newsitem.title: MOROCCO: Moroccan bourse ends session slightly higher.
newsitem.headline: Moroccan bourse ends session slightly higher.

text.p: The Casablanca bourse closed slightly higher on Thursday, lifted mainly by blue-chip shares including Societe Nationale d'Investissement, a market analyst said.
The all-share index traded above 500 points for the second consecutive day, closing at 502.59, up from 500.26 points on Wednesday.
SNI, Morocco's second largest private conglomerate which holds diversified stakes in more than 40 firms, jumped 27 dirhams to close at 602 dirhams.
"Blue-chip stocks pursued their upward trend, pushing higher the bourse index...Demand for liquid stocks remains higher than the offer," a Casablanca-based broker said.
The bourse index registered a performance of 12.4 percent since the beginning of the year, he added.
Banque Commerciale du Maroc, one of Morocco's largest banks, rose two dirhams to close at 712 dirhams.
Leading brewery firm Brasseries du Maroc gained 54 dirhams to close at 1,849 dirhams.
Banque Marocaine du Commerce Exterieur, a very demanded liquid stock, was traded at 460 dirhams, up one dirham over the previous session.
Traded volume on the official market was 65.7 million dirhams, up from 46.6 million dirhams on Wednesday.
